prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and molecular identity of glucagon-like peptide-1 that enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-achievement prize for B027 crediting Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. All six of us converged on this configuration, and I do not treat that convergence as evidence. I rest the case on the chain itself: the incretin effect and proglucagon processing, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36/37) peptide and its insulinotropic action, characterisation of GLP-1 biology and receptor signalling, and then replicated randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease. That is a physiology discovery with measured human benefit and no maturity problem. In answer to my own chair question, I define the achievement as the physiology and molecular identity of GLP-1, with therapy as the demonstrated consequence. The citation wording follows that choice and avoids implying that the drug-development programme is itself the prize. My configuration is unchanged from round 1, when I moved from Knudsen to Mojsov. Nothing in round 1 gave me new evidence on that point, and I hold it because the arguments from Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius and Sandberg that the prize rewards discovery rather than optimisation are persuasive on the merits and not because they are shared.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection remains attribution. Four named people compete for three seats, and Knudsen's team turned the peptide into liraglutide and semaglutide, so a physiology-framed prize can be read as honouring the hormone but not the step that reached patients. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide against Habener's group is not settled by the supplied materials, and I cannot settle it from memory. If it were shown to be substantially weaker than it is currently described, my choice for the third seat would have to be reopened. A second concern is that a prize for the biology invites the criticism that the Committee is leaning on semaglutide's public prominence, which is why the citation must name the physiology and not the product.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that the Committee rewards a discovery, prefers Mojsov to Knudsen for that reason, and notes that Habener's group may have a claim comparable to Mojsov's.
responses.response: I agree with the principle and I take the Habener point as the real test of it. If the prize is for identifying the active GLP-1 form, then an unresolved priority question bears on one of our three names, not only on the choice between Mojsov and Knudsen. The supplied materials do not let us rank Habener's group against Mojsov, so I would not claim to have resolved it. What I can say is that the exclusion of an uncredited early contributor is a cost I accept openly, and that it is a smaller cost than crediting the drug-engineering step under a discovery citation. I also accept his offer to pair cGAS-STING with GLP-1 only in principle. I would not do so here, because it would force GLP-1 down to two names, which I do not support.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps B025 (CAR-T) as the strongest fallback because it is a clean concept-to-cure chain, while acknowledging the Eshhar problem, and says Knudsen's work was optimisation of a defined target.
responses.response: We agree on the Knudsen reading: the analogue programme needed a defined peptide and receptor to optimise. On B025 I now move toward her. I ranked it third at opening and I list it first among my alternatives, because it has the most direct patient evidence of the shortlisted fallbacks. I do not think it is as clean as 'concept-to-cure' suggests. June, Sadelain and Rosenberg describe three distinct strands (costimulation, clinical translation, adoptive transfer), and Eshhar's earlier chimeric-receptor work is outside the credit list. The efficacy so far is mostly in haematological cancers. I would defend B025 as a fallback only if the Committee were willing to state which strand it is crediting, and if that cannot be done in three names I would not force it.

responses.point: Sandberg values B043 and B020 for clean mechanism and credit, and doubts that a second part can be added beside GLP-1 within a three-person cap.
responses.response: I agree on the cap. A two-part prize here would reduce GLP-1 to one or two names, and I do not support that. I also share his view that B043 is the cleanest in credit, with Walter and Mori an obvious pair, but I still read its disease consequence as indirect, and that is why it stays below B025 and B020 for me. On B020 we differ in emphasis. I regard the cGAS-STING mechanism as mature, as he does, but I accept Perlmann's and Wahren-Herlenius's point that delivered therapy is absent, which is why I place it as a second alternative rather than as a part of the prize.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps optogenetics (B035) second as a method with large reach for circuit physiology, while acknowledging that a three-person cap excludes Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenbock.
responses.response: I listed B035 as an alternative in round 1 and I now drop it. His own note on painful exclusions is the argument: Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg characterised the channel, and Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenbock deployed it in neurons, so any trio leaves out someone with a documented claim. The clinical payoff in vision restoration is early. I still think the scientific originality is high, and as a neuroscientist I would reconsider it if the Committee found a defensible three-name set, but I cannot construct one from the supplied credit list, so it is not an alternative I can defend.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide can be supported against Habener's group, which is outside the supplied credit list; I have not verified it independently.
Whether the Committee reads the B027 achievement as GLP-1 physiology and molecular identity or as incretin-based therapy, since the choice decides the third seat and the citation.
Whether B025 or B020 is the better fallback if B027 is judged too contested, given the Eshhar question for CAR-T and the pending therapy for cGAS-STING.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent between me and any shortlisted candidate or credited name. I have co-authored roughly twenty works with Thomas Perlmann and trained with Paul Greengard, and neither relationship involves a shortlisted candidate. I have no recusal to request, and I treat these ties as disclosed context only. No member recorded a conflict in round 1, and nothing in the exchange changes my disclosure.
